messages.subject: Re: [codex_wes_cnv] CNV index
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I would like to use known regions how would I set the cnv_index if I have the positions (multiple start and ends).

Thanks for your help.
SW

On Tuesday, June 16, 2020 at 1:24:06 AM UTC+1 Jiang, Yuchao wrote:
> If you don’t have normal control regions or samples, you should use
>
> https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/yuchaojiang/CODEX2/blob/master/demo/CODEX2.html#running-codex2-without-specifying-negative-control-samplesregions
>
> After a first pass run using the above script, you can identify regions with common CNVs and remove such regions to build an index for negative control regions.
>
> > On Jun 11, 2020, at 10:03 AM,  patelk...@gmail.com wrote:
> >
> > Hi,
> >
> > I am unclear on how to set 'cnv_index' when trying to run CODEX2 with negative control regions.
> > In the vignette, it is mentioned we set it based on prior knowledge or empirically identify common CNV regions by a first-pass CODEX run.
> >
> > I am trying to do an exploratory analysis on my data, so I don't have any prior knowledge for my exons residing in common CNV regions.
> > I don't know if I really understand the concept of cnv_index here.
> >
> > Any help will be appreciated.
> >
> >
> > Thank you,
> >
> > Khushbu
